title: Measuring one part of a system
objectives: Compute a partial-measurement branch and its probability.
Separate conditional predictions from ignored-record marginals.
prerequisites: Chapters 3–5: tensor products, complex amplitudes, unitary gates, Born probabilities and measurement bases.

quizzes.question: For (1,i,1,0)/√3, what is B conditioned on A=0?
feedback: Correct: divide the two-entry branch by √(2/3).

quizzes.question: Can Alice choose her random Bell outcome to transmit a bit to Bob?
options: Yes, by selecting a measurement basis.
No; his unconditioned local statistics do not reveal that choice.
Yes, because their Z results match.
feedback: Basis choice does not change his local marginal.
Correct: conditional correlations require comparison of classical records.
Matching random records are not a controllable signal.
